question: In a homologous series, which element is replaced by any functional group?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Hydrogen**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In a homologous series,** **hydrogen** is typically replaced by a functional group.
 
• A **homologous series is a group of organic compounds that have the same functional group **
 
• It** has similar chemical propertie**s, but they differ by a constant unit, usually a -CH2- group.
 
• The **presence of different functional groups determines the chemical reactivity and properties of compounds in the series.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Homologous Series**

 
 
• We can represent each homologous series by a general formula.
 
• **All the members of a given homologous series possess the same functional group.**
 
• E.g., the functional group of alcohol is a hydroxyl group, and the functional group of aldehydes is an aldehydic group.
 
• **General preparation methods developed for a homologous series** can be implemented to prepare individual members of that series.
 
• The physical properties such as density, melting point, and boiling point of the members of the homologous series show a regular gradation with the rise in molecular mass.
 
• The chemical properties of members of a homologous series are similar though the first member may vary considerably from the rest of the members.
